column1: # work-order.registry.tsv — every place that orders or windows beads by an idiom of its own (ga-9t9acg.1).
# Checked by `python3 -I scripts/work_order.py lint` (run from work-order.selftest.sh). Read the header of
# work-order.sh first: the rule is priority > type > age, and ONE library implements it.
# Columns, separated by ONE TAB each (five, always):
#   kind   consumer  a site that picks "which bead first" (or windows the pool) by itself. The slice named in
#                    `owner` migrates it to work_order_sort and DELETES the row in the same commit. When the
#                    last consumer row is gone the programme is done (reviewed rows stay).
#          reviewed  a line the idioms catch that does NOT order a bead queue (comments, git refs, one story's
#                    own verdict wisp, a report). It stays, with the reason in `note`.
#          ext       a consumer OUTSIDE this repo (engine, panel). Not scanned; listed so the inventory is whole.
#   regex  Python `re.search` over ONE line of that file, comment lines excluded. It has to match at least one
#          line today: a row that matches nothing is STALE and fails the lint, and so does an idiom line that no
#          row matches (UNREGISTERED). So a slice cannot migrate without deleting its row, and a new ad-hoc
#          sort cannot appear without a row that says why.
#   owner  consumer/ext: the slice's bead id, or UNASSIGNED (found after the inventory, no slice yet — it is
#          reported in ga-9t9acg.1 so the Mayor assigns it). reviewed: `-`.
#   note   R-number from docs/research/ga-3zlzot-ordem-unica/inventario-e-desenho.md and what the site does.
# Scope and idioms: see IDIOMS / SCOPE_GLOBS in scripts/work_order.py. The idioms are sort_by on created_at /
# updated_at / priority, any --sort flag, _PILOT_SORT_JQ, Python .sort/sorted keyed on those, and a positive
# --limit (a window taken BEFORE the sort: the ga-g7yt trap).
